extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO and respondents in OED reciprocal disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state-court disbarment or other disciplinary action. Includes notice, opportunity to respond, grounds for exclusion, publication, and post-discipline duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Reciprocal Discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed by the USPTO when a practitioner has been disciplined (e.g., disbarred) by a duly constituted authority of a State; here, Respondent was disbarred by the California Supreme Court, and the exclusion is predicated upon that state action and violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary action by a state authority (such as disbarment) is a recognized basis for reciprocal discipline under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; the Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Opportunity to File a Response
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director sent a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' by certified mail notifying Respondent of the Complaint and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be delivered (certified mail used here) and must inform the respondent of the time period (40 days) and the bases for opposition (the reasons enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)). Timely filing of a substantive response is required to create a genuine dispute of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible Bases to Oppose Reciprocal Discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was given an opportunity to oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the specific reasons from the regulation are not enumerated verbatim on this page, the Notice advises respondents that the regulation lists limited grounds upon which to resist identical reciprocal discipline (e.g., lack of jurisdiction, procedural defects, extenuating circumstances). A timely response must articulate such grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Failure to Respond (Default/No Genuine Issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to file a response to the Notice and Order; consequently, it was determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and exclusion from practice is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to participate (either personally or through counsel) and failure to file a timely substantive response generally results in a finding that no genuine issue exists and permits imposition of the proposed reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy — Exclusion from Practice in Trademark and Non-Patent Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order excludes the Respondent from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reciprocal discipline imposed is identical to the state discipline (here, disbarment) as applied to the scope of practice before the USPTO (trademark and other non-patent matters). The order notes whether the respondent was or was not authorized to practice patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Requirement — Official Gazette Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, the respondent, and the predicate state disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should summarize the basis for discipline (including reference to the state proceeding and specific charges/findings) and inform the public that the respondent is excluded from practice in trademark/non-patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to Other Agencies and Courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office must proactively notify relevant state disciplinary authorities and courts as required by regulation; this ensures dissemination of the discipline beyond the USPTO's own publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's Duties Following Discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not list § 11.58 duties verbatim, those duties typically include obligations such as notifying clients, ceasing practice in regulated matters, and other post-discipline administrative requirements; the respondent must fulfill them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of State Bar Findings as Predicate for USPTO Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order relies on the Office of the Chief Trial Counsel's petition and the California Supreme Court's disbarment order as the factual and legal predicate for USPTO reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State bar disciplinary findings (including counts, defaults, and final court orders) are given weight as the basis for reciprocal action unless successfully challenged under the narrow regulatory grounds for opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to Perform Legal Services with Competence (Cal. Rule 3-110(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTC charged that Respondent willfully violated rule 3-110(A) by failing to perform legal services with competence—specifically, failing to prosecute his client's matter which resulted in the court dismissing the matter for failure to prosecute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of competent prosecution that leads to dismissal is a serious professional misconduct ground that can support disbarment and reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Communicate Significant Developments (Cal. B&P Code § 6068(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTC charged Respondent with violating Business and Professions Code § 6068(m) by failing to inform his client that the lawsuit was dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to inform clients of significant developments (e.g., dismissal of their case) is a clear ethical violation supporting disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Withdrawal from Representation (Cal. Rule 3-700(A)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTC charged Respondent with violating rule 3-700(A)(2) by terminating employment without notice to his client (improper withdrawal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnotified or abandoned withdrawal from representation constitutes professional misconduct and may lead to discipline including disbarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Cooperate in Disciplinary Investigation (Cal. B&P Code § 6068(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTC charged Respondent with violating Business and Professions Code § 6068(i) by failing to provide a substantive response to the allegations in a disciplinary investigation after being contacted by OCTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-cooperation with disciplinary investigations (e.g., failing to respond to inquiries) is independently sanctionable and can aggravate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral Turpitude — Misrepresentation (Cal. B&P Code § 6106)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTC charged Respondent with violating Business and Professions Code § 6106 for moral turpitude — specifically, concealing that his client's case had been dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts of dishonesty, misrepresentation, or concealment that amount to moral turpitude are grounds for severe discipline, including disbarment, and for reciprocal discipline by other tribunals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Release Client Files and Property (Cal. Rule 3-700(D)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTC charged Respondent with violating rule 3-700(D)(1) by failing to promptly turn over his client's papers and property upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention of client files or property after request violates professional obligations and can support disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Disciplinary Decisions for Public Review (FOIA/OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order notes that disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED's FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED maintains public access to disciplinary orders and decisions; practitioners and the public may consult these records for precedent and transparency.
